question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
sql:
WITH months AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT date_trunc('month', CAST(txn_date AS DATE)) as month_start
    FROM customer_transactions
),
customers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_months AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id, m.month_start
    FROM customers c, months m
),
balances AS (
    SELECT cm.customer_id, cm.month_start,
           COALESCE(SUM(
               CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
                    WHEN ct.txn_type IN ('purchase', 'withdrawal') THEN -ct.txn_amount
                    ELSE 0 END
           ), 0) as balance
    FROM customer_months cm
    LEFT JOIN customer_transactions ct 
        ON cm.customer_id = ct.customer_id 
        AND CAST(ct.txn_date AS DATE) <= cm.month_start
    GROUP BY cm.customer_id, cm.month_start
),
monthly_totals AS (
    SELECT month_start, 
           SUM(CASE WHEN balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE balance END) as total_balance
    FROM balances
    GROUP BY month_start
)
SELECT 
    month_start as month,
    total_balance
FROM monthly_totals
WHERE month_start > '2020-01-01'
ORDER BY month_start
